planting.note: Direct sow once soil has warmed after last frost; this tall climbing type benefits from a sturdy trellis or pole support.

directions: Faba Asturiana is a large, flat, creamy-white kidney-shaped dry bean grown in Asturias, Spain, where it is protected as the regional PGI 'Faba Asturiana' and forms the base of the traditional stew fabada asturiana. Plants are tall, indeterminate climbers that need a strong trellis or tall poles to support vigorous vines through the season. Leave pods on the plant until fully dry and papery before shelling, then store the smooth white seeds in a cool, dry place. The thin skin and creamy texture make it prized for slow-simmered bean stews with pork and sausage.
sources: EU eAmbrosia Geographical Indications Register — Faba Asturiana PGI
Fabada asturiana / Fabes de la Granja (regional food heritage documentation)

planting.note: Direct sow after frost danger has passed; grown traditionally as a bush dry bean in Tuscan kitchen gardens.

directions: Fagiola di Venanzio is a small, flattened, mostly white heirloom dry bean cultivated since the mid-19th century near Murlo in the Siena province of Tuscany, Italy. Its very thin seed coat makes it notably quick-cooking and easily digestible once shelled and dried. Harvest pods after they have fully dried and yellowed on the plant, then thresh and store the seeds in a sealed container. The variety has drawn scientific interest for the antioxidant and polyphenol content of its seed extracts.
sources: Finetti et al., 'Phaseolus vulgaris L. var. Venanzio Grown in Tuscany,' Antioxidants journal

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; this indeterminate climbing bean needs tall poles or a trellis for its vigorous vines.

directions: Mongeta del Ganxet is a flattened, glossy white bean with a distinctive hooked shape (ganxet means 'little hook' in Catalan), grown around the Valles and Maresme regions of Catalonia, Spain and protected as a DOP since 2007. Plants are tall indeterminate climbers with white flowers and need sturdy support to carry the season's vine growth. Allow pods to dry fully on the plant before shelling, then store the hooked white seeds for use in slow-cooked Catalan bean dishes prized for their smooth, buttery texture. It commands a premium price in Spain for its distinctive cooking qualities.
sources: EU eAmbrosia Geographical Indications Register — Mongeta del Ganxet DOP
Generalitat de Catalunya DOP product documentation

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; this determinate bush type matures quickly and needs no staking.

directions: Setsetmanera is a small, round, white dry bean grown on the volcanic soils around Santa Pau in the Garrotxa region of Catalonia, Spain, and is one of the traditional varieties covered by the Fesols de Santa Pau DOP. Plants have an upright, determinate growth habit and a notably short cycle, making the crop easy to manage without staking. Harvest pods once fully dry, then shell and store the small navy-type beans, which are prized for their fine flavor and short cooking time. The name references its traditionally fast maturation compared to older local varieties.
sources: EU eAmbrosia Geographical Indications Register — Fesols de Santa Pau DOP
Generalitat de Catalunya DOP product documentation

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; a reliable dwarf bush bean that performs well in cool, damp conditions.

directions: Canadian Wonder is a dwarf bush bean dating to at least 1873, long grown in Canada and popular as a heritage variety in British gardens. The flat, oval green pods can be picked young and eaten as snap beans around 60 days, or left on the plant roughly 90-100 days to mature into red kidney-shaped dry beans. The compact bush habit needs no staking, and the variety is noted for cropping reliably even in cool or wet seasons. Harvest pods regularly for fresh use, or let the final flush dry fully on the plant for storage beans.
sources: Kings Seeds (UK) — Canadian Wonder Dwarf French Bean
Mother Earth News — Heirloom Bean Varieties

common_name: Fagiolo della Regina di Gorga Bean

planting.note: Direct sow once soil has warmed; a vigorous climbing type traditionally hand-sown in early summer and trained on tall poles.

directions: Fagiolo della Regina di Gorga is a pearlescent white, rounded-to-oval heirloom bean grown in the Cilento area of Campania, Italy, around the hamlet of Gorga, and recognized as a Slow Food Presidio in 2018. Vines are vigorous climbers that can exceed several meters in height and need tall, sturdy support. Pods can be harvested green for fresh eating or left to dry fully on the plant before threshing and storing the thin-skinned, quick-cooking seeds. The bean is valued locally for its tenderness, rapid cooking time, and high digestibility.
sources: Slow Food Foundation — Fagiolo della Regina di Gorga Presidio
Italian Wikipedia — Fagiolo della Regina di Gorga

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in fertile, well-drained soil typical of its native clay-loam growing region.

directions: Lingot du Nord is a white, elliptical dry bean with straight, often truncated ends, grown on about fifty communes straddling the Nord and Pas-de-Calais departments of France, where it holds both Label Rouge and PGI status. Pods are left on the plant until fully dry, historically finished on wooden drying racks called 'perroquets' in open air. The beans cook up with less skin separation than ordinary white beans and are noted for a more pronounced, chestnut-like flavor. Shelled dry beans should be stored in a cool, dry place for use in slow-cooked white bean dishes.
sources: INAO (Institut National de l'Origine et de la Qualite) — Label Rouge LA 15/98 Lingot du Nord specification
Semence Mag — Le Lingot du Nord
